items.caption: Tibber Grid Rewards – provides the Grid Reward status (including the 'Delivering' signal) as variables. Requirement: participation in Grid Rewards with a supported device (e.g. Tesla). Complements the 'Tibber V.2' module (official API).

Enter the email address and password of your Tibber app, tick Active and click Apply. Then click “Reload home list” below, choose your home and click Apply again. The connection is established as soon as the status at the top shows “Active”.

Optional but recommended: in the “🔌 Wallboxes” panel, enter the active power data points of your wallbox(es). From them the module works out whether and how much is currently being charged – the basis for the Grid Reward mode and the automations.

Variable “Grid reward mode” (0–3):
0 Normal – no event, car is not charging.
1 Car charging (no reward) – smart charge / forced charging / release: power should come from the grid, not from the battery.
2 Grid Reward: charge (Tibber status “excess”) – grid surplus, rewarded: charge the car AND the battery from the grid.
3 Grid Reward: curtailment (Tibber status “shortage”) – grid shortage: car off, supply the house from battery/PV where possible, minimise grid import.

Panel “🎯 Automations (If → Then)”: every rule checks a condition on a data point of this instance (e.g. Grid reward mode = 2) and, when it occurs, sets up to TWO target variables at the same time – the typical case for a Grid Reward event (e.g. EMS operating mode AND power setpoint in one go). Edge-triggered: a rule fires when the condition becomes true, not again with every data message. The value you enter is converted automatically to the type of the target variable (number, true/false or text). The placeholder “WALLBOX” (upper or lower case) is replaced by the wallbox power currently required and is tracked live as long as the condition stays true – ideal for a power setpoint. Several conditions (AND) or more than two target variables per rule? For that, the “TibberGridRewardTile” tile offers a convenient rule editor with any number of conditions and actions (see its panel “🤖 Show automations”).

Panel “🧪 Simulation (for testing without a real event)”: the buttons trigger each of the three states (available / charge / curtailment) and run through exactly the same code as a real Tibber event – including the automations configured above. “↩ Back to real status” ends the simulation and actively fetches the current real state from Tibber.

Panel “💶 Price curve (official Tibber API)”: optional, independent of Grid Rewards. With an access token (developer.tibber.com/settings/access-token, called “Personal Access Token” there) the module delivers the complete Tibber end-customer price – including any time-variable grid fees (e.g. §14a module 3), not just the pure spot price – as a price curve for price-driven automations/EMS (function TIBBERGR_GetPriceCurve). The convenience variables “Current price” / “Current price level” show the period that is running now; the price level is still Tibber's own classification, not a general assessment – the actual classification for automations should be done uniformly in the EMS. The curve is requested again every 20 minutes so that tomorrow's prices are picked up promptly once Tibber publishes them (usually between 1 and 2 pm); the displayed price itself changes exactly at the change of the hour or quarter hour. With the checkbox “Archive price history” this builds a gap-free price history as the basis for an invoice check.

With TIBBERGR_SetVehicleSetting() a preference (departure time per weekday, minimum charge level, smart charging on/off) can be stored directly in Tibber's own charging algorithm – e.g. from the EMS. There is no form field for it here because the function addresses Tibber's cloud directly, not this module.

Two independent ways to break the Tibber price down into exchange price / procurement / grid fee / taxes – both require the price breakdown to be enabled (checkbox in the panel “🧾 Tariff & grid fees”): the panel itself keeps calculating along for the current price curve; TIBBERGR_DecomposePrice() additionally breaks down a single historical price on request, e.g. for one invoice line.
Panel “🎭 Demo mode”: exclusively for demonstrations/tests – replaces the real price curve with one set via TIBBERGR_SetDemoPriceCurve(). Leave it disabled on an instance that is used normally.
Detailed documentation, examples and background: github.com/DG65/NRGTibberGridRewards.

Optional and independent of Grid Rewards above: provides the end-customer electricity price (including any time-variable grid fees) as a price curve for price-driven automations/EMS. This requires an access token from developer.tibber.com/settings/access-token – it is called “Personal Access Token” there. It is a separate access, NOT the app password from above.

Since 1 October 2025 Tibber has billed quarter-hourly in Germany. “Automatic” requests the finer 15-minute prices and falls back to hourly values if the tariff does not provide them. Only change this if the automatic detection does not give the result you want.

items.caption: Status: determined when the form is opened.

The checkbox above enables archiving of the variable “Current price” – you can also switch it on directly at the variable (in the object tree right-click “Current price” → Archiving). The price is switched exactly at the change of the hour/quarter hour, so the archived history reproduces the price steps with exact timing. IMPORTANT: without archiving there is no price look-back – the function TIBBERGR_GetPriceCurve only returns today and tomorrow, any analysis of the past (invoice check, historical price curve in tiles such as the InverterHub monitoring) is fed from the archive. Recording only starts at the moment you switch it on, nothing is recorded retroactively. The checkbox only switches archiving ON – archiving that was enabled elsewhere is not switched off when you clear the checkbox (otherwise further recording would silently be lost); to switch it off, remove archiving directly at the variable.

Breaks the Tibber end-customer price down into its components (exchange price, procurement, grid fee, taxes/levies) so that a Tibber invoice can be recalculated. Optional, OFF by default (checkbox below) – for everyone who does not need an invoice check this panel has no effect. ⚠️ ALL numbers below (grid fee HT/ST/NT, time windows, base price, discount row) are NOT generally valid but 1:1 the author's own price sheet (E-Werk Netze GmbH, formerly Überlandwerk Mittelbaden) as a format example – before enabling, replace them with the values of YOUR OWN grid operator / Tibber contract, otherwise the breakdown calculates with wrong numbers. The rates that are the same nationwide (electricity tax, levies, VAT) are stored in the module and do not have to be adjusted. The breakdown appears as “components” in TIBBERGR_GetPriceCurve; the total price “price” remains Tibber's authoritative figure.

“To 00:00” means the end of the day (24:00). Windows may span midnight. If a time falls into no window, the work price below applies.

Module 3 does not necessarily apply all year (by law at least 2 of 4 quarters, set by the grid operator per calendar year). In “No” quarters the normal work price applies instead of the time-of-use rates.

items.name: NetzArbeitspreis
items.caption: Normal grid work price when module 3 is inactive in the quarter (ct/kWh net)
These annual amounts do NOT flow into the per-kWh breakdown but into a separate monthly bill. Enter them as an annual value – the module divides it down to the day (/365).

Time-limited discounts/campaigns (e.g. “Tibber base fee discount”). The amount is signed – a discount is NEGATIVE. “Valid from/to” as DD.MM.YYYY (existing entries in the old format YYYY-MM-DD are still read correctly); “to” includes that day, empty = unlimited. Only those active in the billing period are applied.

Mode (variable “Grid reward mode”) as a single value for the EMS: 0 = normal · 1 = car charging without reward (smart charge / forced charging / release → power from the grid, do not discharge the battery for the car) · 2 = Grid Reward charge/excess (charge from the grid + charge the battery from the grid, never discharge) · 3 = Grid Reward curtailment/shortage (car off, house from battery). The price fine-tuning (when to charge/discharge the battery) stays in the EMS.

Rules over the data points of this instance (e.g. Grid reward mode, wallbox charging). As soon as the condition is met, the rule sets up to two target variables at the same time. Edge-triggered – a rule fires when the condition becomes true, not again with every data message. Values are converted automatically to the type of the target variable (number, true/false or text). Placeholder “WALLBOX” = wallbox power currently required, tracked live as long as the condition stays true. The tile “TibberGridRewardTile” can show, manage and switch these rules on/off – and offers an editor there with any number of conditions (AND) and actions per rule.

🔍 Look up values: Symcon lists cannot show a dependent selection list per row (every row can have a different target variable with a different profile). Instead choose a variable here, apply, and click “Show values” – below it all possible values appear, to read off or type into comparison value / value 1/2.

elements.name: PanelSim
elements.caption: 🧪 Simulation (for testing without a real event)

items.caption: Simulates a Grid Reward status and runs through exactly the same code as a real Tibber event – including the automations configured above (so they really are executed!) and the energy counting. This lets you test your own EMS wiring without waiting for a real, often rare event. Important: the simulation stays in place until either the next real status message from Tibber arrives or you click “Back to real status” below – that actively requests a fresh status directly from Tibber instead of waiting for the next message.

elements.caption: The tile display is provided by the separate module “TibberGridRewardTile” (its own instance). All tile settings (colors, font) are found there as well.

items.caption: ⚠️ Do NOT enable on a real, productive instance. Replaces the price curve (TIBBERGR_GetPriceCurve) with one set manually via TIBBERGR_SetDemoPriceCurve() – for demo scenarios (e.g. stepping through cheap/expensive/feed-in surplus), independent of real credentials. As long as this checkbox is off, TIBBERGR_SetDemoPriceCurve() has no effect.
